subtopics.title: The Register and What It Carries

questions.question: The fixed asset register exists because the general ledger:
options: Holds only class totals — it cannot say which asset, how old, how much is left, or whether it still exists

questions.question: A register page carries:
options: Description and identifying detail, purchase date and supplier, cost, method and rate, yearly depreciation, accumulated total, carrying value, location and responsible person

questions.question: The register relates to the ledger the way:
options: The trial balance relates to the journals
The cash budget relates to the income statement
The DEBTORS LIST relates to Debtors Control — detail whose totals must agree with the summary

questions.question: The three uses examiners ask for are:
options: CONTROL (assets produced on inspection), DECISIONS (replace or repair), and AUDIT (every figure traced to a page)

subtopics.title: Acquisitions and What Counts as Cost

questions.question: A machine invoiced at R80 000 with R4 000 delivery and R6 000 installation is recorded at:
options: R90 000 — cost includes everything necessary to bring the asset into use

questions.question: The test separating capital from revenue expenditure is:
options: Does the spending EXTEND the asset's life or capacity beyond its original condition, or merely maintain it?
Whether it was paid in cash
Whether the supplier is registered for VAT

questions.question: Adding routine servicing to a vehicle's cost:
options: Has no effect on the statements
OVERSTATES profit and the asset — and depreciates money that bought nothing lasting
Is required by the matching principle

questions.question: A registered VAT vendor records a fixed asset at:
options: The price plus estimated future repairs
Cost EXCLUDING VAT — the VAT is claimed as input tax and never formed part of the asset's cost

questions.question: Grade 11's part-year rule is that depreciation runs:
options: From the MONTH THE ASSET WAS BOUGHT, pro rata for the months owned in that first year
From the start of the financial year regardless
Only from the second year of ownership
From the date of first repair

questions.question: A vehicle costing R240 000 bought 1 June, year end 28 February, at 15% diminishing balance, charges in year one:
options: R27 000 — R36 000 × 9/12 for the nine months owned

questions.question: In the SECOND year, that same vehicle charges:
options: R36 000, back to the original cost
R31 950 — a full year at 15% of the R213 000 carrying value

questions.question: An asset written down to zero but still in use:
options: Continues to be depreciated at a reduced rate
Has no further depreciation — often a nominal R1 is left standing, and it stays on the register and under control

questions.question: Acquisition controls include:
options: Authorisation appropriate to the amount, quotations obtained, the asset checked against order and delivery note, and the register updated at once
Allowing any employee to order assets
Recording assets only at year end

questions.question: Verification controls require the physical inspection to be performed by:
options: The person responsible for the assets, who knows them best
Someone INDEPENDENT of the person responsible for them, with every difference investigated
The external auditor only, every five years

questions.question: A company vehicle used for family trips is:
options: DRAWINGS whether or not it is recorded as such — the honest treatment is a drawings entry at fair value, or a disclosed private-use policy

questions.question: The pattern running through every asset control is:
options: A document trail, a separation of duties, or a physical count reconciled to a record — all made possible by the register

questions.question: "Vehicles, four hundred and something thousand rand" is useless to the person running the place because:
options: It cannot say which vehicles, how old, which is nearly finished, or whether one has already left

questions.question: The notebook works exactly like:
options: The DEBTORS LIST and the creditors list — one book has the total, the other has the faces, and they must agree

questions.question: If the pages' totals do not match the ledger:
options: Something is recorded in one book and not the other — worth chasing down today rather than next year
The register must be rewritten annually

questions.question: Delivery and installation belong in the machine's cost because:
options: Until it was delivered and installed it could not make a cent — everything needed to get it WORKING is part of what it cost
They are paid at the same time

questions.question: A new engine giving the bakkie another five years is:
options: Buying more asset — it goes onto the bakkie's page and is written down over time

questions.question: The sorting question is:
options: Does this make the thing BETTER or LONGER-LIVED than it was, or just keep it where it was?
Was it bought from a registered vendor?

questions.question: Calling routine servicing "part of the bakkie":
options: Is the safer of the two errors
Makes profit look BETTER than it was, and writes off servicing money for years as if it bought something lasting

subtopics.title: Bought in June, Not in January

questions.question: A vehicle bought 1 June with a year ending 28 February was owned for:
The method is to:
options: Charge a full year and adjust next year
Work out a FULL year first, then take the slice owned — R36 000 becoming R27 000 for nine twelfths
Charge nothing in the first year
Divide the cost by the months owned

questions.question: Slicing only ever happens:
options: In the year something ARRIVES — or the year it leaves
When the method is diminishing balance

questions.question: A machine fully written down but still working:
options: Stays on the register, locked up and somebody's responsibility — a machine finished on paper is still worth stealing
